-If the sample contains elevated levels of immune complexes or other immunoglobulin aggregates, false positive result cannot be ruled out.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE 
1) ds-DNA: Antibodies against dsDNA are specific for systemic lupus erythematosus. Besides antibodies against Sm, they are a serological marker (ACR Criterion) for this disease.
2) Nucleosomes: Antibodies against nucleosomes are detected in sera from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and is especially important in dsDNA negative SLE patients.
3) Histones: Antibodies to one or several types of histones or to the H2A-H2B complex are constantly found in medication-drug induced lupus erythematosus. Histones are also found in 30%-70% of patients with disseminated lupus erythematosus and in 15%-50% of patients with rheumatoid arthritis. In absence of other autoantibodies, especially Sm and dsDNA, is considered a high possible Drug Induced Lupus.
4) SmD1: Antibodies to Sm have a high specificity (~95%) for Disseminated Lupus Erythematosus. Together with antibodies to dsDNA, they can be considered pathognomonic for this condition, but occur in only 5 - 10% of patients.
5) PCNA: Auto antibodies against PCNA (Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen) are specific for systemic lupus erythematosus.
6) Ribosomal P0-protein: These are detected in 10-35% of SLE patients but rarely found in patients with other AI diseases. For this reason, they are considered quite specific for SLE.
7) SS-A/Ro60: Antibodies to SS-A are associated with various Connective Tissue Diseases. The most common occurrence is in patients with Sjogrens syndrome (up to 96% of cases) for which it is considered as a classification criterion. It also reported in SLE, Subacute cutaneous Lupus and other CTDs.
8) SS-A/Ro52: It appears to be more associated with Congenital Heart Block in Neonatal Lupus and with cutaneous lupus manifestations.
9) SS-B/La: antibodies to SSB/La are found almost exclusively in woman in cases of Sjogrens syndrome (50%-70% of cases). In Sjogrens syndrome, combined SS-A and SS-B antibodies mainly occur.
10) CENP- B: Antibodies to centromeres are associated with the limited form of the systemic sclerosis and can be found in ~95% of patients with this form of scleroderma.
11) Scl-70: Antibodies to Scl-70 are found in Up to 65% of patients with progressive systemic sclerosis (diffuse form).
12) U1-snRNP: Anti-U1-snRNP is considered as diagnostic marker of mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD). Used in this indication the antibodies achieve a sensitivity of ~99% and a specificity of ~99%% in absence of both anti Sm and anti-dsDNA antibodies.
13) AMA-M2: High titres of antibodies against AMA-M2 are characteristic of primary biliary liver cirrhosis.
14) Jo-1: Antibodies to Jo-1 are found in polymyositis with a prevalence of 25% - 35%. They are often associated with a concurrent interstitial fibrosis of the lung.
15) PM-Scl: Anti PM-Scl autoantibodies are found almost exclusively in patients with idiopathic myositis and/or myositis overlap syndrome or scleroderma. Approx. 50-70% of patients with Pm-Scl have polymyositis/scleroderma overlap syndrome.
16) Mi-2: Anti-Mi2 is considered as a diagnostic marker for Idiopathic Autoimmune Myositis.
17) Ku: Anti Ku antibodies are detectable in about 5-25% of patients with polymyositis/scleroderma overlap syndrome, about 23% patients with primary pulmonary hypertension, 5-10% patients with SLE.
